title: Evidence versions and publication dates
content: An evidence version identifies a particular edition of repository text. Publication date and retrieval date are separate metadata fields. A recently retrieved document may have an older publication date. A revised document can preserve a link to a prior version while receiving a different content hash. The synthetic corpus uses fixed versions to make retrieval experiments repeatable. Version metadata does not by itself establish freshness for a clinical question. This passage supports searches about document editions and date distinctions. No automatic preference for the newest text is claimed. Synthetic research evidence only. Retrieval relevance != clinical validity.
